course_profile.one_sentence_summary: This course provides a comprehensive theoretical foundation and practical skills in implementing Computer Vision methods, mathematical models, and algorithms using Python.
course_profile.short_summary: Students will explore the classic digital image processing pipeline, including 2D/3D image synthesis, rasterization, vectorization, realistic rendering, and advanced digital processing like segmentation and recognition. Through hands-on Python labs using libraries such as OpenCV, NumPy, and OpenGL, learners will build functional scripts and modules, preparing them for roles in software and embedded development for computer vision systems.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the classic pipeline of digital image processing, from synthesis to vectorization.
Comprehend mathematical models and algorithms for approximation, interpolation, and smoothing (e.g., OLS, Splines, Bezier curves).
Understand models of realistic images, light and shadow models, and the 3D rendering pipeline.
practical_implementation: Implement raw computer vision algorithms using Python libraries like NumPy and Matplotlib.
Develop functional software modules for computer vision tasks using specialized packages like OpenCV, OpenGL, and PIL/Pillow.
Apply base geometric transformations (scaling, translating, rotating, projecting) to 2D and 3D objects.
analysis_validation: Process sensor data for applied tasks such as navigation and autonomous driving.
Perform color correction, filtering, morphological processing, and segmentation on digital images.
architecture_design: Design complex digital image processing pipelines applying software engineering best practices.
Build Python scripts adhering to the principle of incremental functionality development.
research_and_prototyping: Prototype systems for object detection, activity prediction, and scene understanding using modern approaches including CNNs and Deep Learning.

lab_formats: Practical usage of specialized CV and graphics libraries
implementation_tasks: Object identification and image recognition workflows
engineering_practices: Utilization of specialized software libraries (OpenCV, OpenGL)

curricular_relations.from_label: Computer Vision Algorithm Implementation in Python
curricular_relations.reason: Proficiency in Python and its libraries is explicitly required to execute the digital image processing tasks in the labs.
Understanding spatial transformations and projections is foundational for complex 3D scene reconstruction like Structure-from-Motion.
Basic digital image processing (filtering, morphology) is part of the pipeline that leads to advanced object recognition and detection.

what_student_can_understand: The theoretical foundations and mathematical models behind modern computer vision.
The complete pipeline of processing digital images, from raw sensor data to recognized objects.
How rendering pipelines generate realistic 3D scenes using light and shadow models.
what_student_can_build: Python applications that process raster and vector graphics using NumPy, PIL, and OpenCV.
Programs that apply geometric transformations to 2D and 3D shapes.
Software pipelines for image filtering, segmentation, and object detection.
what_student_can_apply: Computer vision techniques for real-world domains like autonomous driving, augmented reality, and significance mapping.
Deep learning concepts for image retrieval and object recognition.
